original_question: If the geodesic flow of a Riemannian metric on the torus T^2 admits an integral that is polynomial of degree 3 in the velocities, then the metric admits a Killing vector field.
target_in_paper: Section 10.2, Conjecture 10.2.1: "If the geodesic flow of a Riemannian metric on the torus T^2 admits an integral that is polynomial of degree 3 in the velocities, then the metric admits a Killing vector field."
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper’s target almost verbatim: it has the correct manifold (the 2-torus T^2), the correct dynamical object (the geodesic flow of a Riemannian metric), the correct hypothesis (existence of an integral polynomial of degree 3 in the velocities), and the correct conclusion (existence of a Killing vector field). It correctly captures Conjecture 10.2.1 rather than the broader odd-degree generalization mentioned afterward.
missing_details: It should specify that "integral" means a first integral of the geodesic flow, i.e. a real-valued function on the tangent bundle T(T^2) that is constant along geodesic-flow trajectories.

To be fully stand-alone, it should say that the polynomiality is in the fiber/velocity variables on T(T^2), and that "degree 3" means total degree 3 (not merely an arbitrary smooth function of velocities).
If one wants exact degree 3 rather than degree at most 3, one should require that some cubic coefficient is not identically zero.
The paper’s conjecture does not impose homogeneity of degree 3; lower-degree terms are not excluded in the official formulation.

The paper’s conjecture does not add extra hypotheses such as flatness, real-analyticity, or functional independence from the energy integral; those belong only to nearby contextual remarks, not to Conjecture 10.2.1 itself.
To avoid vacuity, "admits a Killing vector field" should be understood as admitting a nonzero/nontrivial Killing vector field.

No ambient ring/field choice, positive-characteristic issue, nilpotency condition, auxiliary operator, or "for all sufficiently large m" quantifier appears in this problem; those are not part of the paper’s statement.
refined_question: Let g be a smooth Riemannian metric on the 2-torus T^2. Suppose the geodesic flow of g on the tangent bundle T(T^2) admits a nonconstant first integral F:T(T^2)→R such that, in local coordinates (x^1,x^2;v^1,v^2), F is a polynomial of total degree 3 in the velocity variables v^1,v^2 (so some cubic term is not identically zero). Must g admit a nonzero Killing vector field?
justification: The draft is aiming at the exact statement of Conjecture 10.2.1 in Section 10.2, page 23. I kept the scope exactly there and did not broaden it to the later odd-degree meta-conjecture. The only additions in the refined question are the implicit definitions needed to make the problem stand alone: that an "integral" is a first integral on T(T^2), and that the polynomial is in the velocity variables. I did not add homogeneity, minimal-degree, flatness, analyticity, or independence from the energy integral, because the paper does not include those as hypotheses of Conjecture 10.2.1. This is supported by the paragraph immediately after the conjecture, which separately discusses homogeneous components of analytic integrals, and by the table note explaining what "Degree" means there. The nearby sentence about a Killing vector field producing a linear integral whose cube is cubic explains the intended conclusion and shows why the conclusion must be read as nontrivial.

citations.label: paragraph following Conjecture 10.2.1 (Killing vector field gives linear integral I(ξ)=g(V,ξ), whose third power is cubic)
paragraph following Conjecture 10.2.1 on analytic integrals and homogeneous components
table note after Conjecture 10.2.1 ("Degree" means the smallest degree of a nontrivial integral polynomial in velocities)
